title: The leak scan honours an allowlisted home path, and the placeholder path of the 2026-10-24 BG-23wnhrgc filing is allowlisted, so publish passes that commit
goal: kbcommon.leak_hits skips a home hit whose whole match the allowlist's `home` kind names (lowercased, as for the email and ip kinds), the allowlist carries the three spellings of the Windows placeholder path with the user folder jan that commit bc14f216937a wrote (decoded, JSON-escaped once and twice), and kbpublic.SCAN_FORM is bumped; the commit then passes publish's per-commit leak check, while a real-looking home path is still flagged

run:
import subprocess, sys
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbpublic
old = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "bc14f216937a9ba5d5e412b2c9c9a0cd05b8c9eb:kb/_self/backlog/BG-23wnhrgc.json"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
allow = kbpublic.parse_allowlist(open("_tools/tests_allowlist.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
path = "kb/_self/backlog/BG-23wnhrgc.json"
kept = [h for h in kbpublic.file_hits(path, old, allow) if h[0] == "home"]
real = "/".join(("", "Users", "realperson", "docs"))
still = [h for h in kbpublic.file_hits(path, "see " + real, allow) if h[0] == "home"]
print("home hits the allowlist leaves in the old filing:", len(kept), "| a real-looking home still flagged:", bool(still))
sys.exit(1 if kept or not still else 0)

gates.question: How should publish stop refusing commit bc14f216937a, which is on origin/main and wrote a Windows placeholder path with the user folder jan? (Rewriting or skipping the commit is not offered: it is on origin/main and the projection refuses content, never filters it.)
options: Make jan a generic home name
gates.reason: it is the route the publish design already gives a reviewed value, it names only that placeholder and keeps real-looking paths flagged; making jan generic also lets every later jan path through the scan and the query-log redactor

notes: Why this shape: kbpublic.leak_verdicts allows the allowlist of the commit and of the projection, so a value reviewed and allowlisted later passes the older commits that added it (kb/_self/git.md, Public home). But kbcommon.leak_hits reads the allowlist for secret, ip, email and guid only; a home hit is dropped only by HOME_GENERIC, so no allowlist row can clear it today. Cause of the hit: the home pattern reads the user folder of C:, Users, jan@corp.example.com as the folder jan (the match stops at the @), and only jan.kowalski is generic. The three raw spellings the scan reads in the old filing: decoded, JSON-escaped once (the goal) and twice (the repro string); the allowlist matches the whole lowercased match. Not a rewrite: the commit is on origin/main, publish --rewrite only replaces what was pushed to the public home directly, and the projection never filters content. A later commit already reworded the file (d8609788f9), so HEAD is clean, but publish judges the old commit by what it added. Test: the leak guard is critical, so extend the existing planted-leak test in _tools/test_leaks.py (a home row in the allowlist passes, a real-looking path still flagged), no new test id or file, within _tools/tests_ceiling.json, never a raise. Docs: the docs map names kb/_self/tools.md for _tools/kbcommon.py; at planning tools.md is claimed by BG-xao6jaon (kbtail) and ST-7nuaruwn (bench_load) in sprints SP-7ba3r4ec and SP-3qowbedb, and BG-23wnhrgc (draft, touches _tools/kbcommon.py) is a different defect in the same file: start after those release tools.md, or add the docs when they have landed. If the operator answers the generic-name option, the goal changes to a HOME_GENERIC entry (and the redactor reads it too: _tools/redact.py). After it lands run kbgit.py publish --dry-run on a host with the public remote: a planning scan of the lines added since 2026-10-19 found no other hit than bc14f216937a.
